title: A Ringed Pole-on Outflow from DO Tauri Revealed by ALMA
question: What is the nature of the nested elliptical CO (2-1) rings around DO Tauri, and do they trace a pole-on outflow with measurable ages, mass and energetics?

data.angular_resolution: CO cube from combined configs: 0.21"x0.16"; continuum 0.17"x0.12"

what.value: Disk inclination 28 deg and PA 170 deg

evidence.quote: reporting a low inclination of $28\ensuremath{^\circ}\pm0.3\ensuremath{^\circ}$ and a position angle (PA) of $170\ensuremath{^\circ}\pm1\ensuremath{^\circ}$

what.value: Optical jet blue lobe PA 250+-10 deg; blue-shifted jet velocity 95 km/s

evidence.quote: The PA of its blue-shifted lobe is 250$\ensuremath{^\circ}\pm10\ensuremath{^\circ}$ (cite: 1997Hirth)

evidence.loc: 4.3 CO masses, momentum and energy of the rings
evidence.quote: $\dot{M}_{acc}$ has been estimated as $1.4\times 10^{-7}$ M$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ yr$^{-1}$ and $3.0\times10^{-8}$ M$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ yr$^{-1}$

recipe.goal: Calibrate, self-calibrate and image continuum and CO
recipe.method: ALMA scripts in CASA, continuum self-calibration applied to CO spw; separate continuum from high-res track, CO cube from combined tracks
2D Gaussian in uv-plane with uvmodelfit; inclination from axis ratio for circular disk; image-plane Gaussian for comparison

recipe.goal: Fit ellipses to CO rings channel by channel
recipe.method: Automatic Minuit fit of an infinitely thin elliptical ring maximizing product with channel image; manual fits for blended rings
key_parameters: Errors: +-0.3" manual centers/axes, +-15 deg PA, plus 0.1" and 5 deg added; PA not quoted if eccentricity < 0.35

recipe.goal: Deproject outflow geometry and dynamical ages
recipe.method: Rotate ring centers to outflow axis (PA 253.6 deg), deproject with i=19 deg, t_dyn=R/V with V=V_radial/cos i
assumptions: Outflow perpendicular to disk; wide-angle wind model

recipe.method: LTE optically thin column density, M = mu m_H Omega N/X_CO, velocity corrected by inclination
assumptions: Tex = 25 K, LTE, optically thin; yields lower limits

recipe.method: c_s * Delta t_outburst, outburst 0.2-0.3 of shell interval, T=100 K

evidence.quote: this fit implies an inclination of $19\ensuremath{^\circ}\pm9\ensuremath{^\circ}$
The maximum of the emission of the jet has a PA of $260\ensuremath{^\circ}\pm1\ensuremath{^\circ}$

evidence.loc: 4.3 CO masses, momentum and energy of the rings
evidence.quote: $1.3\times10^{-4}$ M$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$, $1.1\times10^{-3}$ M$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ km s$^{-1}$ and $1.1\times10^{41}$ erg
we obtain an upper limit for the size of the wind/jet outburst launching region of $<10-15$ au
This implies an opening angle of $27\ensuremath{^\circ}$

not_stated_but_needed: Line-free channels and continuum spw selection
Self-calibration solution intervals and imaging parameters (cell, image size, masks, deconvolver, niter, threshold)
How the two tracks were combined (weights, phase centers) and the cube velocity grid
Channel-by-channel image/rms values used to define ring emission for the Minuit merit function
Per-ring area Omega and integration velocity ranges for mass calculation
Selection of points for power-law mass-velocity fits
score_reason: Public data and clear recipe with tables of ring fits, but imaging details and fitting code are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival data, ring-fit table and numeric results; recipe mostly complete though some details missing.
